manifest_row.title: 15 years after Katrina, New Orleans levees are in the best shape ever. Experts say it's not enough.

screening.main_topic: The condition, safety standards, funding, and future upgrades of the New Orleans-area levee and flood-protection system after Hurricane Katrina.
screening.climate_relevance: The article identifies rising sea levels and more intense hurricanes fueled by global warming as reasons existing protection may be inadequate, and discusses planning for flood and storm-surge risks. Climate change is relevant context, but the main focus is levee engineering and risk management.
screening.reason: The text contains meaningful discussion linking global warming and rising sea levels to the need for stronger hurricane and flood protection. However, most of the article concerns the levee system, its standards, financing, and governance rather than climate change itself.
